comment: Seccomp profile shared by all dai/dagster:v2.0 containers in VM4 (dagster-code, dagster-webserver, dagster-daemon). Allows all Docker-default syscalls and additionally blocks a general-purpose hardening baseline (mount, kernel module loading, kexec, cross-process memory introspection, BPF/perf, swap/hostname). NOTE: the 2 outstanding HIGH CVEs for this image (CVE-2026-23949 jaraco.context tar path traversal, CVE-2026-24049 wheel malicious-wheel RCE) are application-layer library vulnerabilities triggered through Python function calls, not through a distinguishable raw syscall -- seccomp cannot filter at that granularity (no syscall uniquely identifies 'extracting a tar/wheel with a malicious path'). The CVE-specific containment for these two findings is implemented at build time in Dockerfile.dagster (pip/wheel/easy_install removed entirely from both system Python and venv, in both bin/ entry points and site-packages, so neither the CLI nor `python -m pip`/`python -m wheel` is reachable) plus the existing docker-compose read_only root filesystem (no LSM/AppArmor/SELinux custom policy involved, per 2026-06-30 decision -- see secure_report/dagster_secure_report.md). This seccomp profile is therefore general defense-in-depth, not a CVE-2026-23949/24049-specific control.

syscalls.comment: Block mount-related syscalls (general baseline; dagster-code/webserver/daemon never need to mount filesystems at runtime)
Block kernel module loading (container should never load kernel modules)

Block cross-process memory access / ptrace (no debugger or process introspection needed at runtime; also closes off a common post-exploitation primitive that an attacker who reached the vendored wheel/jaraco.context code via RCE could otherwise use)
Block BPF and perf events (privilege escalation / info leakage primitives, not used by dagster-webserver/code-server/daemon)
Block swap and hostname changes (not needed by any of the 3 dagster containers)
Block obsolete/legacy syscalls not needed by dagster (oprofile dcookie lookup, legacy NFS server control, x86 vm86 mode). General attack-surface reduction.
